Disappointing Return to L'Usine Dong Khoi
Mar 2020
L'Usine Dong Khoi used to be one of my favourite restaurants - trendy decor, great vibe, delicious hot food. I returned recently, nearly a year on and found that the restaurant size had been reduced from its former New York restored factory industrial chic style, to a rather dark and somewhat depressingly decorated small very narrow basic cafe. I was the only customer which was a complete turn around from many previous visits where you would be lucky to find a table. The waiters and waitresses are still very helpful and friendly but there were quite a few annoying errors on this recent visit. I asked for a soda water with lemon juice and asked if the lemon juice could be squeezed and put into a jug rather than arrive with just a can of soda and some token lemon wedges. The waitress said that she would arrange it. However the drink arrived as a can of soda with 2 small wedges of lime. Again, I asked pleasantly if the juice could be squeezed in the kitchen and this time, when she arrived with the lime juice, it was plentiful and brought out in a small jug. I ordered a full English breakfast and asked if my sausage could be well done all over and when asked how I preferred my eggs, I asked for sunny side up. The bacon was truly delicious when it came, cooked to perfection and much better size and texture than the usual streaky bacon in other restaurants. The sausage was lightly cooked and under-cooked in parts, though in fairness was still very tasty. The grilled tomato was not grilled enough and was almost cold. The egg yolks were very firm and overcooked and not what was expected at all. Finally, I had ordered extra baked beans which were stone cold on my plate and I asked if they could be heated up. When they returned they tasted home made and were very tasty indeed . However, they were chock a block with diced up bacon mixed in everywhere, which I felt was unnecessary as they were delicious enough anyway but I couldn't help wondering how vegetarians or vegans would react if they ordered baked beans as nothing on the menu indicated that they came with bacon bits. The waitress came with 2 sunny side eggs just before I left as she said she had noticed my egg yolks were very hard. I thought this was a lovely touch and characteristic of the helpful pleasant waiting staff which is part of the L'Usine experience. I just think that the changed size and ambiance has lessened the attraction of the Dong Khoi branch and even though I was the only customer, there was total indifference as to trying to produce a meal that was hot all over. I will be calling in occasionally at the D2 branch which is usually quite full, and definitely to the smart buzzy D7 branch which is now my firm favourite.
